cards.text: Friend, we're opening a letter! It's from Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, and he names our brother Sosthenes right alongside him, writing to the church of God in Corinth. And look, he puts his name right up top, not like those texts that just say 'hey' from a number you never saved.

cards.question: Paul says he became an apostle of Christ Jesus by his own choice.

cards.text: Paul doesn't just call them a church. He tells them who they are: sanctified in Christ Jesus and called to be holy.

cards.question: Paul's greeting in his letter to the church in Corinth is for the Corinthians alone and nobody else.

cards.text: Paul widens it to all those everywhere who call on the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, their Lord and ours. That's a group chat with NO member limit, and Paul greets the whole chat with grace and peace!

cards.question: Paul sends the church in Corinth grace and peace. Who does he say the grace and peace come from?

answers.text: God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ
All the churches of Christ everywhere

cards.text: Next, Paul says he ALWAYS thanks his God for them. ALWAYS, friend, and I can't even always remember where I set down my own timer.

cards.question: Paul thanks his God for the Corinthians because of the grace God has given them in Christ Jesus.

cards.text: Paul says that in Christ they've been enriched in EVERY way. Friend, the richest thing in my old junk drawer was an expired coupon, and it still carried itself like a millionaire.

cards.question: Paul names two ways the Corinthians have been enriched in Christ. What are they?

answers.text: In all speech and all knowledge

cards.text: Paul tells them why it happened: "because our testimony about Christ was confirmed in you."

cards.question: Because of all this, Paul says the Corinthians do not lack any ___ gift.
With every spiritual gift, the Corinthians are eagerly waiting. What does Paul say they're waiting for?

answers.text: The revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ
Paul's next visit to their city
A letter from the church in Rome

cards.text: Not snooze-button waiting, friend, EAGER waiting. And Paul says He will sustain them to the end.

cards.question: Paul says He will sustain the Corinthians to the end so that they will be blameless on the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.

cards.text: Then Paul points them to God Himself, the One who called them into fellowship with His Son Jesus Christ our Lord. And Paul hangs every promise he just made on Him.

cards.question: Paul hangs all his promises to the Corinthians on God. What does he say about the God who called them?

answers.text: God who called them is faithful
God will judge them by their knowledge
God will send Paul back to them

findings.problem: The card says Paul 'greets the whole chat with grace and peace,' which decides who the 'you' of 1:3 is: everyone who calls on the Lord's name. The text leaves that open. Card 6 then says Paul sends grace and peace to 'the church in Corinth,' so the two cards contradict each other.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't share the fact's core action. Paul always thanking God is about being faithful and consistent. Forgetting where the timer was set down is about memory, so the comparison doesn't click. It also reads more like a nice dad being pleasant than a real laugh.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: 'Paul says He will sustain the Corinthians' leans on 'He' from card 14, which is no longer on screen. Read alone, it sounds like Paul says that he himself will sustain them. The question should give enough context without naming the subject the text leaves open, for example 'Paul says the Corinthians will be sustained to the end so that…'.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Card 16 and the question both say Paul 'hangs every promise' on God. That points straight to a trait you can rely on, 'faithful,' and rules out the two wrong answers, which are future actions rather than something promises could rest on.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The answers aren't the same kind of thing. The right answer states who God is ('God who called them is faithful'). Both wrong answers state what God will do ('will judge them by their knowledge', 'will send Paul back to them'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
